verifications.claim: Artemis II reentry and splashdown live coverage begins around 6:30 p.m. EDT (3:30 p.m. PDT) on Friday, April 10, 2026.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '6:30 p.m.: NASA+ coverage begins'; R5: 'Live coverage begins at 6:30 p.m. EDT'; R7: 'NASA+ coverage kicks off at 3:30 p.m. PT'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state coverage begins at 6:30 p.m. EDT / 3:30 p.m. PDT on April 10, 2026.

verifications.claim: NASA is streaming the Artemis II return to Earth on NASA+, YouTube, and social media.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'streamed live on NASA+, the NASA app, and its YouTube channel' 'Follow NASA on social media'; R2: 'Watch live return coverage on NASA+... social media'; R5: 'NASA+ streaming service and YouTube'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly confirm NASA streaming on NASA+, YouTube, and social media.

verifications.claim: Artemis II return to Earth is expected around 8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT).
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: '8:07 p.m.: Splashdown'; R2: '8:07 p.m. EDT (5:07 p.m. PDT)'; R5: '8:07 p.m. EDT'; R6: '5:07 pm' PDT equiv.; R7: '8:07 p.m. ET'
verifications.reasoning: Exact time and time zone conversion directly supported across multiple sources.

verifications.claim: Netflix and Prime Video are also hosting the stream, according to WIRED.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R6 (WIRED): 'streaming platforms such as Amazon Prime, Apple TV, Netflix, and HBO Max'
verifications.reasoning: WIRED (R6) directly lists Netflix and Amazon Prime as hosting the stream.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule will enter the atmosphere at approximately 4:53 p.m. PDT.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R3: 'reentry to begin at approximately 4:53 p.m. Pacific time'; R7: 'around 4:53 p.m. PT, when the Orion spacecraft hits entry interface'
verifications.reasoning: Sources precisely state atmospheric entry at 4:53 p.m. PDT for Orion.

verifications.claim: The Orion capsule will experience a 6-minute communication blackout.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'planned communications blackout expected to last about six minutes'; R3: 'lose communication for about six minutes'; R6: 'six-minute communications blackout'
verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly confirm ~6-minute blackout for Orion.

verifications.claim: Live high-definition coverage shows the plasma fireball.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R3: 'agitating the air... into a fireball' 'livestreaming reentry'; R2: 'plasma built around the crew capsule'; R4: 'Watch the Artemis II re-entry: Separation, blackout, then splashdown'; R6: 'plasma blanket'
verifications.reasoning: Sources mention live coverage of reentry, plasma/fireball during blackout phase, but no explicit 'high-definition' or confirmation of live visual of fireball (blackout blocks signals).

verifications.claim: Live high-definition coverage shows parachute deployment.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R2: details '8:04 p.m. ... drogue parachutes... three main parachutes deployed'; R3: 'two small parachutes will deploy... larger chutes will deploy' with livestream context
verifications.reasoning: Live coverage of reentry/splashdown includes parachute phase per timelines, but no 'high-definition' specified.

verifications.claim: Live high-definition coverage shows the final splashdown in the Pacific Ocean.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Will Artemis II splashdown be livestreamed'; R2: 'SPLASHDOWN!' live updates; R3: 'NASA will livestream... splashdown'; multiple confirm live streams of splashdown
verifications.reasoning: All sources confirm live streaming of splashdown, but no explicit 'high-definition'.

verifications.claim: The capsule will land off the coast of California.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California'; R2: 'off the coast of San Diego'; R3: 'splashdown off the coast of San Diego'; R5: 'off the coast of California'

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'final day of their 10-day milestone mission'; R2: 'approximate 10-day mission'; R4: '10-day mission'; etc.
verifications.reasoning: Consistently described as 10-day mission across sources.

verifications.claim: The final stages take place in daylight, notes WIRED.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: R6 (WIRED): 'San Francisco: 5:07 pm' (implies daylight in April, but no mention of 'daylight')
verifications.reasoning: WIRED provides time (5:07 p.m. PDT, daylight hours), but does not note or mention 'daylight'; attribution to WIRED unsupported.
